method: expanding-window pseudo-out-of-sample interval coverage; reduced-form BVAR predictive bands with parameter and shock uncertainty (posterior draws x stochastic paths), percentile intervals on the LEVEL of each series
limitations: Estimation uses final revised data (pseudo-, not real-time).
Coverage is on series levels in transformed model units.
Consecutive-origin outcomes overlap, so the effective number of independent observations is well below the origin count.
No Covid dummies in the headline block, matching rolling_evaluation.json -- but every published forecast IS estimated with them; use 'production_spec' for the bands that are actually shown.

coverage_standard_error.note: Binomial standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/n) at the NOMINAL level with n = 50 origins, quoted so a measured coverage is not read as exact. Origins overlap, so the number of independent observations is well below n and this understates the true sampling error.

production_spec.description: same evaluation with the six Covid dummies (2020Q1-2021Q2) that every published forecast estimates with; this is the model whose bands are actually shown

band_scale_factors.derivation: k(h, level) = z(nominal) / z(empirical), z(p) the standard-normal quantile at (1+p)/2; multiply each band half-width by k around the median. k < 1 narrows an over-covering band.
band_scale_factors.caveat: Measured on series LEVELS in transformed model units. Published fans show year-on-year growth, whose forecast error at h > 4 is a difference of two level errors, so these factors are an approximation there. Apply the production_spec factors to a published fan; the headline factors describe a model with no Covid dummies.

calibration_holdout.method: per level/horizon/variable k = z(nominal)/z(empirical) refitted without the scored origin (leave_one_out) or on origins whose outturn was already observed (rolling_origin, the real-time scheme; first 12 usable origins per horizon not scored); the band half-width is scaled by k around the median and the outturn scored against it
calibration_holdout.caveat: Consecutive origins share outturn quarters, so leave-one-out still leaks neighbouring information and is optimistic; rolling_origin is the honest number. Measured on series levels in model units, like the factors themselves.

conformal_calibration.method: split-conformal: per level/horizon/variable the band half-width around the median is scaled by the ceil((n+1)*level)-th smallest of the n past band stretches (outturn distance from the median over the half-width on that side); rolling origin, so origin i uses only origins whose outturn was observed at i; first 12 usable origins per horizon not scored. The whole distribution is recalibrated the same way level by level for the PIT histogram and CRPS.
conformal_calibration.verdict: not adopted: out of sample the conformal 90% band covers within sampling error of the Gaussian-k band (0.824 vs 0.822, s.e. about 0.05), at a wider average width and a worse CRPS, and it narrows bands with a history of small errors (bank_rate 68% coverage 0.39). Forecast misses cluster in time (2019-22), which violates the exchangeability the method relies on; the fix is a model with time-varying volatility (issue #12 option 1).
conformal_calibration.caveat: With 12-48 past origins the 90% factor is a high order statistic (the 12th of 12 at the start), so one extreme outturn sets it until enough later origins arrive. Consecutive origins share outturn quarters. Levels in model units.

pit_histogram.note: share of scored outturns per PIT decile; calibrated = 0.1 each. Pooled over variables and horizons.

crps.note: quantile-score CRPS over tau in [0.025, 0.975], mean over scored origins and horizons, model units; ratio < 1 means the recalibrated distribution scores better
